_comment_firestore: An ARRAY, because the project has more than one database and rules are per-database. `firebase deploy --only firestore` with the single-object form publishes to (default) alone, silently leaving `staging` on whatever it was created with — the app then reads a database whose rules nobody has updated. Each database names its own rules file so the two can diverge; they are identical today, and `npm run rules:diff` says whether that is still true. The indexes are shared, since a query that needs an index in one database needs it in the other.
_comment_storage: An ARRAY, for the same reason `firestore` above is one, and it bit us the same way. The project has two buckets — the default one and `recomp-48b7b-staging`, which is what NUXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET points at outside production. The single-object form has no `bucket` field to name, so `firebase deploy --only storage` published `storage.rules` to the DEFAULT bucket alone and silently left staging on the deny-all template the console creates a new bucket with. Every chat attachment in staging failed with `storage/unauthorized`, and nothing in the deploy output said so. Both buckets are named here, and both read the same file: unlike the Firestore pair there is nothing about a bucket that wants to diverge, and a second rules file is a second thing to forget to point at a bucket. Add the bucket here when you add a bucket.
